result:
Round 308 is closed and round 309 is ready to dispatch. The decision is **CONTINUE**.

**Round 308 result.** C passed all 10 rows with real browser checks, found no bugs, and the gate published commit `738df73`. The click test (CONT-1 and CONT-30) ran 6 valid times each with no click.
- PERF-COMMIT-RESCHEDULE is closed on that evidence. The rewiring stage it would have needed is not opened.
- The gate reviewer's one Low (doc 224 points at evidence outside the repo) and one suggestion (an exact count in one test) go to the deferred Low list. The other suggestion is attached to an existing note, to be done before anything starts using the unused code.
- `tasks/round-308.md` is an exact copy of the old task.

**Round 309 = PERF-4a: faster loading of public audio previews and cover images from the R2 worker.**
- **What I measured at HEAD in real Chromium:** browsers cannot reuse a preview they already have (no ETag). Every reload and every seek in a preview downloads all 5.76 MB again, and range requests are ignored.
- **On my scratch copy of the change:** a reload costs 0 bytes (304). A seek downloads about 0.98 MB instead of 5.76 MB. A range past the end of the file now gets a proper error (416) instead of the whole file.
- **Tests on the scratch copy:** 57/57 worker tests pass, and each of the 8 deliberately broken versions makes at least one test fail.
- **What A changes:** both worker copies (`workers/r2-proxy.js` and `cloudflare/r2-worker.js`, with an identical helper block), new test rows PR1–PR9 in `workers/r2-proxy.test.mjs`, and a new doc 225. The routes for purchased files (studio, download, recordings, originals) must stay byte-for-byte the same, and the 7 protected files are untouched.
- **What C checks:** the worker in real Chromium (judged by the server log), the old worker as a control so the probe can tell the two apart, the 57 worker tests, and the anonymous `/studio-lab` and sign-in guard on both screen sizes.

**PERF-4 is split into three stages; nothing is dropped:**
- **4a** is this round.
- **4b**, caching purchased Studio stems, waits on your answer below. It also needs the sign-in token moved out of the file URL, and that code is in a protected file, so it goes into SRW-21-PLAN.
- **4c**, permanent cache keys that never change, needs a change to the upload pipeline, which is not in this repo. It is recorded as a backend handoff.

**Things to know:**
- **`npm run verify` does not run the worker tests,** so the gate does not cover this round's main tests. Until root adds `node --test workers/r2-proxy.test.mjs` to `verify` (I filed ROOT-REQ-VERIFY-WORKER-TESTS), C runs them itself.
- **Deploying the worker is outside the loop.** Production stays unchanged until you deploy it. Doc 225 will list the checks to run afterwards, including a seek in Safari, which can't be tested here.
- **A product-page check can't run in the cloud:** the mock API serves local previews, not worker URLs. It is kept as later evidence.

**Questions for Saba:**
- **SABA-Q-PERF4-STUDIO-CACHE:** should a buyer's browser keep purchased stems on disk, checked against the buyer's purchase every time they reopen, so reopening is faster? Or should it keep re-downloading them so nothing stays on a shared computer? That is today's behaviour.
- **SABA-Q-WORKER-DEPLOYED:** which worker copy is actually live? Once known, a small task can remove the other copy.

The performance-optimizer and tech-lead agents agreed on 4a. On Studio caching, one would allow it and the other would not; I kept today's behaviour and put the choice to Saba. The advisor was used twice: before writing, and as a final review, whose three fixes are in the task.

The next regression round is due on or after 2026-11-05, and the next RETRO is at round 320. No new architecture checkpoint was requested; the three earlier requests are still unanswered and don't block.

All B artifacts are in `b-round-308/` in the loop folder (frozen list `b-round-308-r309-tree-sha256.txt`).
